Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: SIG Q17 clarification needed - key ownership scope

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for working with us on the SIG. One of our reviewers flagged Q17 ("Does your company use customer-managed keys for data at rest? If yes, provide details of key hierarchy and separation of duties.") as ambiguous for Redwood's deployment options. Specifically the reviewer wants to know whether this question should be answered only for customer-managed KMS (private deployment) or whether we should also include details about service-managed keys used in Redwood-hosted runs (hosted API).

Could you confirm your recommended interpretation (answer for all modes vs. per-deployment) and, if possible, provide a concise sentence we can include in our SIG summary and an evidence artifact (diagram or policy) that demonstrates the distinction? I've attached the snippet from the SIG for quick reference.

Attachment: SIG_Q17_excerpt.pdf (snippet)

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our internal deadline for finalizing SIG answers is next Tuesday.

Regards,
Aidan
Security Engineer
Oxbridge Payments

Hi Aidan,

Thanks for the clear call-out and the attached excerpt. Quick answer up front: we recommend providing a per-deployment answer in the SIG (i.e., explicitly state the distinction between Redwood-hosted service-managed keys and customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated). That gives your reviewers the granularity they want and avoids conflating our service key handling with customer-managed KMS setups.

Proposed one-line wording you can paste into the SIG: 
"Redwood supports both service-managed encryption keys for hosted API workloads (keys held and operated by Redwood) and customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated deployments; where customer-managed keys are used, customers retain key custody and control (see KMS ownership diagram and policy)."

We can join a short sync if you'd like — I'm free tomorrow 10–11am PT. Marissa / Kimberly, can you confirm the current best-evidence artifacts (diagram + policy) and whether we have an SOC-2 excerpt that maps to Q17?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Security & Compliance (Programs)

Priya / Kimberly — quick internal notes for the reply and artifacts: 
- Evidence: we have an internal KMS ownership diagram (kms-diagram.png) that shows the two flows (hosted: service keys in HSM managed by Redwood; private: customer KMS control plane).
- Policy: the "Key Management and Custody Policy" contains the separation-of-duties language; latest signed version is signed-key-policy.pdf (we can provide redacted copy).
- SOC 2 mapping: control CC-22 (encryption and key management) maps to SIG Q17; we can extract the narrative as a short excerpt for the SIG answer (we've done this for other customers).

Draft suggested longer answer (for our records / final editing):
"Redwood uses service-managed encryption keys for hosted API workloads (data encrypted at rest with keys stored in Redwood-managed HSMs). For Private/Dedicated deployments, customers may configure customer-managed keys (CMK) via their cloud KMS, retaining ownership and rotation control; Redwood provides integration guidance and audit hooks but does not possess the customer CMK private material. Separation of duties between key custodians and operators is enforced by role-based access and by access-controlled key escrow procedures described in the Key Management Policy."

I can produce a short redacted SOC-2 excerpt and pull the diagram into a one-page PDF. Will aim to have artifacts by EOD tomorrow.

-M
